claim: For two task-distinct hypotheses with legal scalar Gaussian responses N(f_i(x), sigma^2), sup_x |f_0(x)-f_1(x)|=Delta<infinity, and both errors <=delta<1/2, every adaptive learner has E_0[N] >= (2 sigma^2/Delta^2) kl(1-delta||delta). If Delta=0, acquisition is impossible. The costed form uses sup_x KL(P_0^x||P_1^x)/cost(x).
interface: Adaptive legal scalar evaluations; fresh independent Gaussian noise; bounded stopping or integrable stopping with truncation argument.
proof: Stopped-transcript KL chain rule: query selection contributes zero conditional KL; each response contributes <=Delta^2/(2 sigma^2); binary data processing lower-bounds transcript KL by kl(1-delta||delta).
cost: Expected query count and optional query cost; input/answer bits and decoder computation remain additional charges.
baseline: All adaptive strategies are covered; a finite known separated class has a nearest-residual upper bound in robust_observability.md.
falsifier_or_boundary: Pair f_0=0 and f_B(x)=2^-B x on [0,1] has degree one but requires Omega(sigma^2 4^B) calls at fixed confidence. Exact hitting does not imply noisy margin.
unresolved: Efficiently acquire a robust design and margin for general succinct formula/predictive classes
External proof and novelty review

claim: For F_(D,H)={0} union {c x^k: c=a/b reduced, 1<=a,b<=H, 0<=k<=D}, legal rational x in [0,1], Gaussian scalar noise sigma, and supplied D,H, the minimax adaptive query count to identify the exact predictive function at error delta<=1/4 is Theta(1+sigma^2 max(H^4,H^2 D^2) log(1/delta)) at the report's explicit sufficient answer precision O(log H+log D).
interface: Noisy scalar evaluations at chosen rational points; target coefficient and degree withheld; overall finite grammar and global caps supplied.
acquired: exact coefficient and degree, hence predictive class
proof: Two probes x=1 and x=D/(D+1) give a two-coordinate code with minimum L-infinity gap Delta=min(H^-2,1/[3H(D+1)]). Gaussian concentration gives upper bound. Near adjacent rational constants and adjacent degrees give adaptive KL lower bounds matching both H^4 and H^2D^2 terms.
cost: Calls are tight at sufficient answer precision; query coordinate bits, response bits, clipping, output code, and finite codebook decoding are explicitly charged in the leaf. Minimum precision Pareto frontier remains open.
baseline: A nonadaptive two-anchor experiment attains the minimax adaptive order; a strongest same-class adaptive learner cannot asymptotically improve call order.
falsifier_or_boundary: Without a global height or degree envelope, arbitrarily close distinct monomials prevent every fixed finite uniform guarantee. The theorem does not cover arbitrary rational functions or unknown noise.
unresolved: Minimum input/output precision and complete query-precision Pareto frontier
External novelty/priority review

claim: For exact oracle O_r(u)=chi_u(Q(r)), complete legal profiles agree iff Q(r)-Q(r') lies in intersection_u ker(chi_u). If the desired task differs on a common fiber, every deterministic/randomized adaptive learner has pairwise error >=1/2 under a uniform prior, at any query budget.
interface: Exact algebraic query maps; any legal query set and answer functionals.
acquired: only the quotient class visible to the oracle
proof: Fiber characterization is the definition of the joint observation map; couple both worlds with identical learner randomness and induct on transcript queries.
cost: Information cost is infinite for a task label not constant on fibers; targeted added matrix query includes input and full matrix output bits.
baseline: No adaptive procedure can beat the fiber obstruction; 2x2 matrices separate c[x,y] for c in {0,1}.
falsifier_or_boundary: Over an infinite field, scalar points identify the commutative abelianization, so this does not make commutative PIT impossible. Over F_q with base-field-only queries, 0 and x^q-x are formally distinct but observationally aliased.
unresolved: Universal finite-dimensional query families for broad rational formula classes
No noise-stable universal matrix query claim

claim: For stationary two-state binary HMMs with r0=1/(8L), r1=1/(2L), emissions correct with probability 3/4, training restricted to independent length-3 episodes, and target the endpoint Y_(3+L) after a fresh length-3 context, constant expected-TV risk requires Omega(L^2) training episodes; adjacent-pair testing identifies the pair in O(L^2), matching the exponent.
interface: Passive independent fresh stationary episodes, each truncated at three observed symbols; no hidden-state labels/interventions/conditional oracle.
acquired: which HMM and its exact endpoint predictor
proof: Length-3 KL is O(L^-2), while average endpoint forecast kernels after context are separated by a positive constant. Le Cam/triangle-risk lower bound; adjacent observation pair has mean gap 3/(16L), so Hoeffding gives O(L^2).
cost: Omega(L^2) reset episodes and 3 symbols per episode. Rank/emission/pair-Hankel margins stay constant; minimum transition probability is Theta(1/L).
baseline: Pair-correlation threshold test is the matched two-point upper baseline; oracle-supplied realization has zero further acquisition cost only because it supplies the missing model identity.
falsifier_or_boundary: Does not lower-bound one uninterrupted stream, one-step prediction, or HMMs with stated fast-mixing/positivity parameters.
unresolved: Independent audit of constants
Arbitrary-HMM minimax and uniform mixing dependence

claim: For L>=126, the supplied pair of stationary binary HMMs r0=1/(8L), r1=1/(2L), with emissions correct at 3/4, has minimax training-symbol cost Theta(L) for constant expected-TV prediction of Y_(3+L) from an independent fresh 3-symbol context, when training is one uninterrupted stream. A concrete predictor has risk <=c/8 using T=5179(floor(0.85L)+1) symbols, where c=(3/4-exp(-1))/8; if T-1<=c^2 L/8, every learner has max risk >=c/4.
interface: Known two-model family and L; only model index withheld. One uninterrupted stationary observed training path, followed by an independent fresh length-three evaluation context. No hidden-state labels or intervention oracle.
acquired: model index and its endpoint forecast
proof: For lag s=floor(0.85L), the product W=Y_tY_(t+s) has model means separated by at least d*=(0.7875-exp(-0.84))/4. Products from disjoint adjacent blocks are iid; Hoeffding with B=5179 makes model error <=c/8. For the lower bound, KL of a length-T observed stream is <=(T-1)/(2L), evaluation-context KL <=9/(4L^2), and the two forecast kernels have expected-TV gap >=3c/4. Pinsker and bounded-loss change of measure give max prediction risk >=c/4 below the stated T threshold.
cost: Exact-output upper: T=5179(floor(0.85L)+1)=O(L) symbols, one training start, O(T) scan, O(1) memory; forecast output may require O(L log L) bits and O(log L) growing-integer multiplications. For a rounded forecast at the same epsilon0=c/8 risk, use B=5879 to allocate c/16 to classification and c/16 to rounding; output uses O(1) bits and controlled powering uses O(log L) multiplications with O(log L) guard precision. Lower bound is Omega(L) symbols. Evaluation context adds three symbols and one start.
baseline: On the same pair/loss, independent length-three reset episodes have matching Theta(L^2) symbol complexity. Independent reset episodes of length Theta(L) match the one-stream Theta(L) symbol order; the stream adds only savings in charged episode starts.
falsifier_or_boundary: Two-model, fixed-noise, fixed-risk theorem only; it does not establish a rank-agnostic or arbitrary-HMM guarantee, an optimal leading constant, or a gain over long reset episodes. Rank and pair-moment margins remain constant while minimum transition mass is Theta(1/L).
unresolved: External proof and novelty review
Generalization to unknown-state or general HMM classes under explicit mixing assumptions

claim: For finite-rank process f with complete witness block H_L, supplied rank cap R and column incoherence mu0, adaptive uniform-row completion from exact rational prefix queries discovers the unknown exact rank and a word basis, with independent held-out residual checking and full-block fallback. The successful-panel query bound is O(N R^(3/2) mu0 log(R/delta)+rN+validation), where N=|Sigma^{<=L}|.
interface: Adaptive exact rational scalar queries f(w) for observable prefixes; not passive sample access or full matrix outputs.
proof: Krishnamurthy-Singh random-row sequential column detection with exact residuals; every appended column is genuine, and an independent random row panel detects any remaining outside-span column with high probability. Finite Hankel pivot factorization yields a realization.
cost: Exact cell queries, basis storage, rational bit growth and arithmetic are charged in the leaf. If R=N or panel size >=N, no sub-full-block saving. No singular gap needed for exact oracle; noisy completion needs additional off-span margin and sampled-basis conditioning.
baseline: Direct full-block rank/elimination costs N^2 cells and O(N^3) field ops; a basis-supplied oracle costs O(qr^2) shift entries but is stronger; both are compared explicitly.
falsifier_or_boundary: Without C_L no finite transcript certifies all future behavior; without useful R cap adaptive query advantage vanishes. The incoherence lemma source applies to matrix column spaces and process-specific lower bounds remain incomplete.
unresolved: Rank-free stopping/cap removal
Noisy trajectory-oracle robust adaptive basis discovery
External proof/priority review

claim: Two rational orthonormal dictionaries can be distinct modulo signed permutation and have zero coherence, condition number one, bounded atoms and two-sparse coefficients of magnitude >=5/13, yet induce the same full process law. Every source-only adaptive learner then has I(dictionary; transcript)=0; if a later task predicts atom 1, the source-only mean squared error is >=1/65 under a uniform two-world prior.
interface: Full raw source trajectory access or any adaptive scalar functional of its law, including exact population means.
supplied: dictionary candidate worlds and source process law
later task asks for atom-indexed behavior
acquired: observable source predictor/subspace may be learned; intended latent dictionary is not
proof: Explicit orthogonal rotations give different sparse bases for the same target Y=R1 and therefore identical data distribution; couple source trajectories and learner randomness. The later-task floor follows the squared-distance midpoint identity.
cost: Zero source information for any query/sample budget; side information is at least one bit for the two-world label, or later labeled task data are needed.
baseline: Full-data baseline has the same zero information; source prediction itself is solved by the invariant predictor R1.
falsifier_or_boundary: Not an impossibility for canonical bases, invariant predictive subspaces, or multi-task sparse-code models with additional coefficient-distribution assumptions.
unresolved: Positive predictive dictionary acquisition under multiple task/normalization assumptions

claim: A complete finite Hankel block with sigma_r>=gamma and controlled empirical/rounding/SVD error supports unsupplied-rank thresholding. Uniform exact rank recovery fails without a gap (small-mass two-component mixture). All-future basis certification fails without a witness horizon/rank cap (delayed finite clock aliases any finite transcript).
interface: Independent reset trajectories or exact/noisy prefix probability queries on a declared finite block.
supplied: block completeness/witness horizon for all-future statement
error bound and, for noisy rank selection, singular margin
acquired: rank of the chosen finite block and truncated observable subspace
proof: Hoeffding plus Weyl perturbation and cutoff at 2R; two-point mixture and delayed-clock counterexamples show necessity of margins/horizon.
cost: Explicit N trajectories, observed symbols, pq storage/SVD, b-bit rounding and certified numerical error in spectral_unknown_rank.txt.
baseline: Nested-rank holdout validation and retained sample-frequency lookup receive same data and can outperform exact algebraic-rank selection on prediction risk.
falsifier_or_boundary: Finite-block rank is not an all-horizon realization if completeness is absent; rank gap alone does not bound long products or recovery conditioning.
unresolved: Adaptive finite-sample basis acquisition with no rank/horizon and robust stability

claim: In the specified persistent noisy one-hot atom class, q+1 subset queries with O(beta^-2 log(q/delta)) repeated readouts recover the hidden atom/null class and an exact all-horizon finite-state predictor with probability >=1-delta. A fixed q-bit group-test bank matches costs; the same-data best-policy baseline can simulate the learner.
interface: Controlled subset-membership queries and persistent latent parameter; not passive fixed-feature moments.
proof: Hoeffding confidence intervals separate the active/null response; prefix or bit group tests recover index; model law is explicit product conditional on the index.
cost: q+1 calls, repeated noisy symbols, query descriptor bits, O(q) model code; exact cost ledger and finite 72-case check in leaf.
baseline: Nonadaptive group-test bank matches the same query/symbol order; strongest equal-interface policy can copy all learner state.
falsifier_or_boundary: Does not give a general algorithm for arbitrary unenumerated observables or an advantage over equally informed same-interface policies.
unresolved: Generalization beyond the controlled one-hot class
External novelty review

claim: For a finite controlled HMM, if active and randomized assignment policies coincide on every reachable logged observable-history-conditioned action distribution and use the same reset/observation/stopping schedule, transcript laws and estimator risks are identical. In a separate one-sided-erasure pulse model, physical excitation can reduce expected cost versus idle-only passive sampling after action cost; adaptivity has no gain versus the best precommitted allocation with the same actions.
interface: Logged controls; known action and cost schedule; hidden state remains hidden in pulse example.
supplied: controlled HMM class and action policies
proof: Sequential kernel induction proves transcript equality; pulse result uses first informative emission probability per cost and exact stopping-cost lower bound.
cost: Action, emission, reset and stopping costs are explicit in leaves; action counts alone do not establish equivalence.
baseline: The strongest matched randomized assignment has the same full action allocation; idle-only passive baseline is weaker because it lacks excitation right.
falsifier_or_boundary: Hidden-state clamps are a different interface; equal action counts do not suffice; feedback may matter with noisy sign flips or state-persistent dynamics.
unresolved: Adaptive action advantage in persistent-hidden-state noisy HMMs with matched allocation

claim: Against a retaining baseline permitted to compute and keep the same representation from the same source transcript E under equal memory/computation/query limits, no transfer learner using S=phi(E) has an information or simulation advantage. A strict net gain needs a named narrower baseline or real resource constraint and must include acquisition, failed search, validation, storage, and downstream costs.
interface: Equal source transcript and later workload; declared resource vector or scalar cost.
supplied: same downstream task/input and resource accounting
proof: The retaining policy can run the same phi and copy the learner's state/update rule; scalar break-even follows by adding one-time acquisition and per-task reuse costs.
cost: Acquisition+reuse compared against retained-data re-learning; storage, validation, failed branches, coding and arithmetic charged.
baseline: Best equal-information retaining/simulating policy; narrower baseline must be named explicitly.
falsifier_or_boundary: A real memory cap, preprocessing deadline, or restricted query/output interface can create a practical tradeoff; no empirical performance gain is asserted.
unresolved: Demonstrate an end-to-end gain against a competent, matched retaining baseline

claim: A stationary finite-state target P_(epsilon,m) can be epsilon-close in whole-process TV to one-state source Q while its exact causal-state count is m+1 rather than 1. Literal source-machine reuse has target-supported conditional TV error 1 on the rare component, though average actual-path error is epsilon.
interface: Exact source law is acquired, then reused unchanged on a shifted target law; target provides actual finite histories.
supplied: target shift class and future-horizon loss
proof: Mix all-zero process with epsilon mass on an m-cycle with disjoint support; exact causal classes follow from different infinite futures.
cost: Source machine O(1) state work; target exact machine needs m+1 states or a phase counter; no net amortization claimed.
baseline: Target-specific acquisition/validation can detect the rare component at cost depending on epsilon and m; not computed as a break-even result.
falsifier_or_boundary: Not an ergodic target and not a uniform-mixing counterexample; expected risk vanishes with epsilon. This attacks exact state-count/worst-case conditional stability only.
unresolved: Stability under fixed-state, irreducible, uniformly mixing and support-overlap assumptions

claim: Given a size-s noncommutative rational formula over Q, exact full-matrix output oracle with explicit UNDEFINED status, and the public N51 rational affine-pencil hitting-list theorem, center acquisition plus an injective finite residual feature map and BFS closure recovers a valid affine matrix-inverse descriptor for the formula equivalence class. It preserves the original inverse-gate domain. Query bound Q<=L0+(1+kR)L1+R with k=nd^2 and R=(s+1)d.
interface: Exact full matrix-valued evaluation at legal matrix tuples; matrices of several charged dimensions; original undefined status.
supplied: formula class/size/variable count and coefficient field Q
acquired: valid formula descriptor on original domain
proof: Domain-preserving affine linearization gives residual series dimension <=R. A feasible-pencil hitting list makes the residual feature map injective; breadth-first residual closure builds minimal realization of that perturbed generic-entry series. Quotient invariance plus block-triangular specialization proves the learned descriptor remains defined on the original syntax-tree domain.
cost: Q full-matrix calls; max dimension Dmax<=max(d0,d(R+1)R e1); at most Q Dmax^2 returned rationals, with polynomial exact height under a supplied rational height h. Full input/output bit and exact elimination costs are charged in the leaf.
baseline: If the formula tree is given, direct evaluation is one formula traversal; descriptor acquisition only helps if formula is withheld and reusable descriptor is the target. N68 sparse-polynomial acquisition is a different known-sparsity interface.
falsifier_or_boundary: The learner is conditional on the hit-list theorem, not practical. It is not syntax-tree recovery or minimal affine descriptor for Phi; x^-1 example has a d-dimensional residual series for a one-state formula. All-field extension is only local unreviewed; no noisy version.
unresolved: Independent verification of N51 list theorem/generator and whole descriptor learner
Practical constants and finite-noise robust acquisition
All-field validity and historical priority

claim: For a complete finite p-by-q Hankel block of rank r with unknown r, an entry-only Bernoulli word-event oracle supports adaptive row/column CUR acquisition and unknown-rank cutoff with a high-confidence stopping test, provided left/right coherence, sampled-core gap, entry precision and residual-leverage bounds hold. The learner can return UNKNOWN or full-block fallback when the certificate does not pass.
interface: Each selected word query returns a fresh independent Bernoulli indicator for whether a reset episode begins with that word; only one chosen word event is observed per oracle call.
supplied: finite block/witness completeness for process-level rank
target error/confidence and numeric oracle model
acquired: factorized CUR approximation with certified operator error
proof: Random row/column sampling with matrix Chernoff yields span coverage; Weyl/Wedin perturbation controls sampled core and CUR error; fresh uniform residual cell tests reject underfit candidates using a residual-leverage promise and phasewise failure spending.
cost: Training samples per selected word, validation samples, precision, core arithmetic and full-block fallback are charged in adaptive_hankel_acquisition.txt. No trajectory-sample saving follows against a raw path oracle because each path exposes all prefixes.
baseline: Full-block spectral estimation on the same entry-only law may query all block cells; against raw reset trajectories the full-block baseline shares the same sampled data and CUR only changes compute/storage.
falsifier_or_boundary: Without a useful gap or residual leverage, rank and underfit residual can be hidden; rank cap/witness horizon is still required for all-future realization. CUR output need not be a positive or exactly Hankel-compatible process.
unresolved: Independent source/proof audit
A robust sample-optimal learner under a legal passive trajectory oracle
Remove residual-leverage or sampled-core-gap assumptions

claim: For the explicit finite HMM pair whose known witness history h has probability p=q^T and conditional next-bit laws Ber(1/2±delta), n passive length-(T+1) episodes have exact KL n p d(delta), d(delta)=2delta log((1+2delta)/(1-2delta)); constant-error testing needs Omega(1/(p delta^2)) episodes. A conditional-sample oracle callable at h before the learner observes h removes the p factor; an exact law evaluator uses 1-2 queries but must resolve joint probability scale p delta.
interface: Three distinct contracts: passive reset observations, named-history conditional samples, exact full-law probability queries.
supplied: known finite HMM construction and witness h
proof: The episode laws differ only on event h; exact TV/KL scale by p. Conditional samples expose the continuation directly. Exact joint probabilities encode the contrast in a p delta-sized answer.
cost: Passive expected witness count k/p and emitted symbols, conditional sample count Theta(delta^-2 log(1/alpha)), law-query precision > log2(1/(p delta)) bits are explicit.
baseline: Chernoff/majority tests on equally informed observations; conditional oracle is stronger because it skips history generation.
falsifier_or_boundary: If the policy must observe h before querying conditionally, its expected p^-1 wait remains; exact evaluator with additive error larger than p delta loses the constant-query advantage.
unresolved: General HMM class and state/horizon discovery costs

claim: For every T and delta in (0,1/2), two explicit stationary irreducible aperiodic finite-state HMMs with 2^T context states have identical laws on every observation block of length <=T yet their next-symbol conditional laws differ by TV 2delta at every supported T-context. Under passive episodes capped at T, exact minimax expected-TV risk is delta regardless of sample count.
interface: Stationary passive trajectories truncated at T, arbitrary number of independent episodes; next-symbol forecast after observed T-context.
proof: A binary de Bruijn shift context chain has uniform stationary contexts; transition bias depends on the oldest context bit, which has not appeared in <=T-block laws. Pointwise midpoint predictor attains risk delta; common transcript law gives matching lower bound.
cost: No amount of capped passive samples or numeric precision resolves it; one extra observation or one exact on-support conditional-probability query identifies sign. Hidden-state count 2^T and mixing time Theta_delta(T log T) are charged.
baseline: Constant midpoint predictor is minimax; length-(T+1) likelihood test has Chernoff rate from the leaf.
falsifier_or_boundary: Exponential state count and growing mixing time; not a fixed-state or uniform-fast-mixing lower bound.
unresolved: Lower bound under fixed state count, bounded mixing, or a longer accessible horizon

claim: For a known one-hot length-d weighted-automaton family with N=n^d candidate words, amplitude Delta, per-call excitation cap E, Gaussian noise sigma and selectable midpoint comparator, adaptive point-query identification has minimax query order Theta(N+N sigma^2/(Delta^2 E)(1+log(1/delta))) for delta<=1/4. No-hit and zero-reference KL lower bounds match a pairwise tournament. A richer signed dense-group interface reduces high-SNR calls from N to log N while transmitting N weights per call.
interface: One named word scalar query with per-call excitation; separate richer dense linear-sensing interface; threshold/finite response bits are part of the contract.
acquired: hidden word index and exact automaton
proof: Point query lower bound combines probability of ever hitting unknown coordinate with an adaptive zero-reference KL sum; tournament gets matching rate. Dense signed halves implement binary search under a different vector-query contract.
cost: Calls, total excitation, query addresses/weight vector, response bits and evaluation work charged separately; exact finite verifier covers only noiseless fixtures.
baseline: Matched adaptive point tournament and signed group search; compressive binary search is neighboring prior art.
falsifier_or_boundary: Fixed quantizers without useful midpoint can alias; dense-query call advantage ignores N-entry query bill; not a general unknown WFA theorem.
unresolved: General WFA or HMM family learning
Noisy finite-bit Pareto frontier under a fixed quantizer

claim: For the supplied one-path template over {0,1,#}, where the hidden target is L_w=Pref(w#) for a word w of length at most H and M=2^(H+1)-1 candidates, exact nonadaptive membership requires exactly M-1=2^(H+1)-2 calls, while adaptive membership uses H+1 to 2H calls and hence has optimal order Theta(H). If membership addresses are instead sampled IID from a designer-chosen distribution before labels, exact-label minimax cost is Theta(M log(1/delta)) for 0<delta<1/4, without an additional log M factor. The minimal DFA size |w|+3 and real Hankel rank |w|+2 are hidden and recovered from w.
interface: Scalar membership oracle for named strings x in {0,1,#}*. The class template and horizon cap H are supplied; target word w is hidden. Nonadaptive queries are fixed in advance. Passive IID addresses are sampled independently of labels and target. Equivalence-oracle access is a distinct stronger contract.
acquired: target word w and exact semantic predictor f_w
minimal DFA and Hankel rank for this supplied template
proof: Membership-positive sets are laminar subtrees and terminal singletons, so q fixed addresses induce at most q+1 response patterns; terminal queries for all but one target attain M-1. An adaptive prefix walk uses at most two calls per level; information needs at least ceil(log2 M)=H+1. For exact passive IID labels, target-specific certificates of at most three addresses give O(M log(1/delta)); a parent-child edge with query mass at most 3/(M-1) gives the matching lower.
cost: Each response is one bit. Adaptive address lengths total O(H^2) symbols, stores O(H) bits. The exact fixed schedule has M-1 calls and Theta(H 2^H) literal address symbols. Passive IID sample count is Theta(M log(1/delta)) and mean address length Theta(H), so address symbols are charged separately. A favorable equivalence oracle can return w# in one call, but that payload is Theta(H) symbols and requires teacher-side target search.
baseline: Best exact fixed nonadaptive membership schedule is M-1; best exact adaptive order is Theta(H); exact-label passive IID membership is Theta(M log(1/delta)). A stronger equivalence query to {epsilon} can reveal the full target as counterexample w#, but is not a unit-cost membership query.
falsifier_or_boundary: The path-transition template is supplied. This does not establish arbitrary weighted-automaton, HMM, or unknown-Hankel-basis acquisition. The exact adaptive constant remains H+1<=Q<=2H; no novelty or priority claim.
unresolved: Exact optimal adaptive query count within H+1 to 2H
General hidden-basis discovery without a supplied path template
Novelty and external proof review

claim: For the same supplied one-path membership template with independent known BSC(epsilon) labels and 0<epsilon<1/2, every passive IID address distribution and every delta-correct learner requires n >= (M-1) kl(1-delta||delta)/(3 d_epsilon), where d_epsilon=(1-2epsilon) ln((1-epsilon)/epsilon). A uniform-address traversal learner uses O(M (1/2-epsilon)^(-2) log(H/delta)) noisy passive samples. The log H gap is unresolved. Adaptive noisy membership has an information lower bound of order H/[1-h2(epsilon)] and a repeated-prefix-walk upper O(H (1/2-epsilon)^(-2) log(H/delta)).
interface: Same membership addresses as A18, with independent known BSC(epsilon) answer noise. Passive address schedule is a designer-chosen target-independent IID distribution; adaptive schedules may depend on previous noisy answers.
proof: For each parent-child edge, the two languages differ on only the child prefix and the two terminal queries for parent and child. Any address separates at most three edges, so some edge has mass <=3/(M-1); its per-sample KL is at most 3 d_epsilon/(M-1). Binary data processing gives the lower. Uniform-address sampling with repeated majority labels along the recovered path gives the upper. Adaptive lower follows from BSC channel capacity and Fano; majority repetition in the prefix walk supplies the upper.
cost: Noisy passive upper is O(M g^(-2) log(H/delta)) samples, g=1/2-epsilon, with mean address length Theta(H) and separately charged address symbols. The lower charges one noisy bit per membership answer. Adaptive upper is O(H g^(-2) log(H/delta)) calls; each address has length at most H+1.
baseline: Matched best designer-chosen passive IID distribution for the lower; uniform support over all nonempty binary prefixes for upper. Adaptive uses the same BSC answer channel with sequential prefix queries.
falsifier_or_boundary: Only independent BSC noise with known epsilon and supplied one-path template. Passive log H factor and active noisy-query constant/channel gaps are not sharp; no theorem for arbitrary predictive systems.
unresolved: Remove or prove necessary the passive log H upper factor
Sharpen active noisy-query constants and compare to optimal noisy search
External proof and priority review
